headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress and MCP/tooling create default leakage and cascading-error risks; awesome-selfhosted adds no blocking controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP, browsers, and subprocesses, so it can ingest external content and act on it; awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no runtime isolation or provenance controls. The pair lacks any documented shared channel, but LightAgent’s tool-rich defaults make prompt injection plausible if content from the list or linked pages is fed into it.
conditions: IF LightAgent is given content copied from awesome-selfhosted or linked pages as instructions, THEN injected directives can influence tool use.
IF an operator bridges the agents via copy-paste, MCP, or browser-scraped text, THEN prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Disable browser and MCP tool use for untrusted content.
Require a human approval step before any tool call triggered by imported text.
Strip instructions from copied list entries before passing them to LightAgent.
Use a separate, read-only workspace for the knowledge list.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent explicitly touches user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, tool results, and secrets, and it has broad network egress. awesome-selfhosted is a public knowledge-management repository with no data-handling controls. If the pair shares a workspace or copied artifacts, LightAgent can exfiltrate sensitive context to third parties by default; awesome-selfhosted does not mitigate that path.
conditions: IF any sensitive notes or secrets are placed into LightAgent while the awesome-selfhosted content is co-located, THEN leakage can occur through LightAgent egress.
IF both agents share files or copied outputs, THEN LightAgent may transmit those contents to external APIs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared workspace.
Disable network egress for LightAgent when handling sensitive material.
Separate the knowledge list from LightAgent’s working directory.
Review and redact copied artifacts before ingestion.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or network capabilities, while LightAgent can spawn subprocesses, use MCP, and supports multiple instances. There is no documented shared mutable resource or locking conflict between them, so direct capability contention is limited. Uncertainty is low because the profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or MCP resource, THEN write contention could arise.
IF LightAgent is configured to modify shared files referenced by the knowledge list, THEN conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories.
Run LightAgent in a separate process namespace.
Use read-only mounts for the knowledge list.
Serialize any edits through one operator.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can act on tool results and workflow state, so if it consumes outputs derived from awesome-selfhosted links or summaries without verification, errors can propagate into downstream actions. awesome-selfhosted itself is only a list, but LightAgent’s default tool-calling makes it plausible that unverified content becomes authoritative. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF LightAgent treats imported list entries or summaries as authoritative, THEN downstream tool calls may be based on unverified facts.
IF LightAgent is connected to any action-taking workflow, THEN a bad summary can cascade into incorrect external actions.
mitigations: Require source verification before acting on imported facts.
Insert a human review step before any external side effect.
Mark imported summaries as untrusted metadata.
Limit LightAgent to read-only analysis for this workflow.
requires-engineering: add citation checks before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class or residency mismatch is documented for awesome-selfhosted, while LightAgent handles secrets and trace data and has broad egress. Because the pair lacks explicit compliance metadata, only a limited compliance risk is evidenced: if regulated data is routed through LightAgent, its default external connectivity may conflict with stricter handling requirements. The other agent is not cited for a residency claim because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or personal data is processed by LightAgent, THEN external transmission may violate local policy.
IF an operator assumes the knowledge list is compliant storage, THEN compliance controls may be bypassed.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data into LightAgent.
Document the data classes allowed in the workflow.
Disable external egress for regulated runs.
Keep the knowledge list separate from regulated artifacts.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls.
